title: First Foresight
next_chapter_hook: Why does the blurry figure of the young woman in the foresight seem so familiar? Those eyes, so identical to his own—could this be fate's guidance, or a maze laid out by the Eye of Heaven?

text.content: The night was as dark as ink. In the corner of the Tianqing Sect Servants' Quarters, an oil lamp flickered, casting Chen Ji's thin silhouette in shifting lengths. He sat cross-legged on a straw mat, and the pale golden mark between his brows was faintly burning, like a brand reminding him—instantly, fate had become inextricably tangled with the Forbidden Fragment.

Chen Ji lowered his gaze, his fingertips gently touching the mark between his brows, which emitted a faint glow. He could sense the fragment's presence deep within his Mental Sea—quietly suspended, golden text flickering like a dormant fierce beast awaiting awakening. Three hours of foresight—this was the ability the contract granted him, but also a sword of Damocles hanging above his head.

dialogue.content: "Young man, don't act rashly." Mo Xiansheng's voice came from the fragment, aged and weary. "Heavenly Fate is the foundation of existence; five points of consumption is no trivial matter. This old one observes your fortune—today marks your first use, and there may be strange phenomena. Remember—act within your limits."

text.content: A faint smile curved Chen Ji's lips, and on that usually timid and dull face, a rare trace of anticipation appeared. He murmured, "Disciple understands." With that, he took a deep breath, his spiritual sense slowly probing into the Mental Sea, sending a thought to the fragment—"Activate."

In an instant, the world seemed draped in a thin veil. The servants' quarters before Chen Ji's eyes began to fade and distort, everything becoming illusory and ethereal, only the golden mark between his brows growing increasingly scalding. He felt himself passing through some invisible barrier, falling toward a future moment.

Wind howled past his ears, and when he opened his eyes again, he was in another scene—the Outer Court Training Grounds of Tianqing Sect, sunlight blazing. Dozens of servant disciples had formed a circle, and inside, two people faced off with drawn swords. One was Zhang Tieniu, a notorious bully of the outer court, the other was Li Tieshui, an honest and timid soul.

"You trash, daring to snatch my spiritual grass?" Zhang Tieniu kicked Li Tieshui in the abdomen, the latter stumbling backward but not daring to fight back. The surrounding crowd burst into laughter, no one lending a hand. Chen Ji watched coldly, taking all of this in—this was something that would happen about one hour later.

The foresight continued. Chen Ji saw Li Tieshui kicked to the ground, blood at the corner of his mouth, yet clutching the hemostasis grass in his arms. Zhang Tieniu cursed and was about to deliver another kick when a clear shout came from outside the crowd—"Stop!" Su Qingyao's figure appeared at the entrance of the training grounds.

dialogue.content: "So that's how it is..." Chen Ji murmured in the foresight. He saw Su Qingyao drive Zhang Tieniu away and help Li Tieshui up; he saw the unwilling look in Zhang Tieniu's eyes as he slunk away; and he saw, after the crowd dispersed, Li Tieshui alone, his fists clenched tight and hatred burning in his eyes.

text.content: Just then, searing pain struck without warning! Like ten thousand silver needles piercing his brow center simultaneously, Chen Ji groaned, the foresight image twisting violently. He saw Su Qingyao turn her head, her gaze piercing through time and space, locking directly with his—those clear, cold beautiful eyes distinctly flickered with scrutiny and suspicion.

"Return!" Mo Xiansheng shouted sternly. Chen Ji's spiritual sense tensed sharply, and the illusion before his eyes shattered like broken glass. When he came to his senses, the oil lamp in the servants' quarters still flickered, yet his forehead was covered in cold sweat, a thread of crimson seeping from his nostrils—those five points of Heavenly Fate had indeed been paid in flesh and vital essence.

choice.prompt: The headache was splitting; the five points of Heavenly Fate had been depleted through the nosebleed. Chen Ji wiped away the bloodstains, gazing at the dim oil lamp, his heart churning with complex emotions. Should he stop here, or...?

choices.text: Take the opportunity to rest and digest this experience first
choices.description: The consumption has been so severe; recklessly trying again may damage the foundation.
choices.risk_hint: May miss the chance to verify more details

text.content: Chen Ji endured the excruciating pain, slowly closing his eyes to regulate his breathing. He began recalling every detail from the foresight—time, place, characters, expressions... This was not merely peeking at the future, but a precise intelligence operation.

choices.text: Strike while the iron is hot; immediately verify the foresight's accuracy
choices.description: One hour later at the training grounds—let's see if this spectacle unfolds as foreseen.
choices.visible_reward: Verify the ability's effectiveness and build confidence
choices.risk_hint: If the foresight is wrong, it will severely shake confidence

text.content: Chen Ji gritted his teeth and stood up, supporting himself against the wall to steady his body. One hour later, the Outer Court Training Grounds—he must witness this prophecy with his own eyes. Even if it's just an illusion of verification, he must see it.

One hour later, the training grounds. The crowd had formed a circle, the scene inside matching the foresight to the letter—Zhang Tieniu's arrogance, Li Tieshui's timidity, that kick, that smear of blood... Chen Ji stood in the shadows at the outermost edge of the crowd, taking it all in, a barely perceptible smile curving his lips.

Then Su Qingyao appeared. Her timing, her words and demeanor, were identical to the foresight. Chen Ji's pupils contracted, sweat beading in his palms—what did this mean? It meant he truly could foresee all variables within three hours, that he possessed a forbidden artifact capable of reversing heaven and earth.

However, just as Chen Ji prepared to slip away, an inexplicable palpitation struck suddenly. His brow center heated up again, and the fragment in his Mental Sea trembled on its own, rippling with eerie patterns. A blurry image flashed by—there, in the shadows at the corner of the training grounds, a young woman's figure was watching him.

The girl's face was unclear, as if shrouded in a layer of mist, but those eyes—those eyes made Chen Ji feel an窒息般的窒息。His heart seemed clutched tightly by an invisible hand, instinctively wanting to see clearly, yet only feeling his head splitting, the world spinning.

choices.description: Regardless of any cost, I must see whose eyes those belong to.

text.content: Chen Ji gritted his teeth tightly, his spiritual sense surging madly into the fragment. Yet the image remained blurry, and instead a nameless will counterattacked from within that mist—cold, scrutinizing,居高临下，仿佛天道之眼正透过时空注视着他。

choices.text: Immediately retreat, avoid alerting the enemy
choices.description: Today's consumption has been too great;不宜再冒险。那身影迟早会再次出现。
choices.visible_reward: Preserve strength; come prepared next time
choices.risk_hint: That figure may disappear from now

text.content: Chen Ji suppressed the churning in his heart and quietly withdrew from the crowd. What he didn't notice was that in the corner of the crowd, a young woman with a light veil over her face was gazing in the direction of his departure, a meaningful smile forming at the corner of her lips.

dialogue.content: "Remember this feeling." Mo Xiansheng's voice rang out in his Mental Sea, carrying a hint of gravity. "Every foresight is proving your existence to Heaven. Today's first trial, just a small test, is of no great consequence. But if used too frequently..." He paused. "The Eye of Heaven will eventually lock onto you."

text.content: When Chen Ji returned to the Servants' Quarters, the sky had begun to lighten. He lay on the bed, his body feeling as if emptied, yet a unprecedented flame burned in his heart. The Tianji Record was real, the foresight ability was real—therefore, everything was possible.

He closed his eyes, and those blurry eyes appeared again in his mind. Who was that? Why did they feel so familiar? Chen Ji always felt that gaze concealed something he had forgotten for a long time, a stirring deep in his bloodline, an emotion called "obsession," quietly breaking through the soil.

Footsteps of early-rising servants came through the window. Chen Ji opened his eyes, the excitement and confusion on his face gradually receding, returning to that dull, timid expression. No one knew that after tonight, on this waste servant's chessboard, the first piece had already been placed.
